Cracks in the Concrete

A photo essay about Humans and Nonhumans on Georgia Tech's Campus
By Ishaan Marwaha November 16, 2026

Every day at Georgia Tech, we move through a campus built for humans, with glass buildings, metal benches, and concrete paths laid out for sheer efficiency. The trees, grass, and wildlife around us rarely get more than a passing glance. 

The photographs that follow in this photo essay look closely at those overlooked spaces, where human design meets the nonhuman life that shares our campus. As you move through the four sections, notice who seems to be in charge of each space, and whether that changes along the way.
